# Dīghītikosalajātaka (Ja 371)
**ID:** Ja 371
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Dīghītikosalajātaka
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/ja371
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Dīghītikosalajātaka* (Ja 371) is a birth story set at Jetavana, where the Buddha recounts it in response to the contentious monks of Kosambī [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1883]. The narrative tells of King Dīghīti of Kosala, who relinquished his realm and went into exile to avoid warfare and bloodshed against the king of Kāsi [Yu Xue 2004]. After the king and queen were ultimately captured and executed, their son, Prince Dīghāvu—identified in the concluding *samodhāna* with the Bodhisatta—had the opportunity to kill the rival king in revenge [Appleton 2014; Fausböll 1883]. Remembering his parents' counsel that violence cannot be overcome by violence, Dīghāvu spared the king's life, transforming enmity into reconciliation and regaining his ancestral throne [Appleton 2014; Yu Xue 2004; Fausböll 1883]. In Burmese epigraphic and art-historical records from the Pagan period, the story is depicted under variant titles including *Kosalarāja Jātaka* and *Dīghatissa* [Win Than Tun 2002; Ray 1946].
Scholars note that while the Pāli Jātaka identifies Prince Dīghāvu with the Bodhisatta, a Chinese Jātaka collection instead identifies the father with the Bodhisatta and the prince with Ānanda; the variation and the absence of bodhisatta identifications in older canonical contexts indicate that the story was likely not a jātaka originally [Anālayo 2010].
Curated parallels recorded by SuttaCentral include canonical accounts in the *Kosambakakkhandhaka* of the Vinaya (Kd 10), the *Upakkilesa Sutta* (MN 128), Ja 428 (*Kosambiyajātaka*), Dhammapada verses (Dhp 3–5, Patna Dhp, and Udānavarga parallels), the Mūlasarvāstivādivinaya, and Chinese parallels such as MĀ 72, EĀ 24.8, and the *Liudu ji jing* [SuttaCentral; Appleton 2010; Trung Huynh 2016]. DharmaNexus confirms extensive cross-language reuse, aligning the text with the Sanskrit *Kośāmbakavastu*, Sanskrit and Tibetan versions of the *Udānavarga*, and Pāli reuse in the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* and *Nīti-gantha-saṅgaho Caturārakkhadīpanī* [DharmaNexus].

- Resembling parallels (SuttaCentral): MA 72 長壽王本起; SHT Sutta 75; EA 24.8 長壽; SF 13; Lzh Mi Kd 10b b. Kosambaka Khandhaka; Lzh Mg Bu Vb Pc4 Ukkoṭana; Lzh Dg Kd 9 Kosambaka Khandhaka
